_what_this_is: Gold-standard Tier-G Ingredient KB entry for soy isoflavones / genistein — the ADR-002 quality bar and the drop-in shape for aurora_ingredient_research_kb.ingredient_profile_json (v2-lite + additive Tier-G fields). Codex backfill of other cohort actives mirrors this; human random-sample QA checks against it.

ingredient.what_it_is: Plant phytoestrogens from soy. Genistein and daidzein bind estrogen-beta receptors in skin and act as antioxidants — the active firming story behind many 'collagen' and 'tofu' K-beauty creams.

marketing_vs_reality.reality: The firming comes from soy isoflavones signaling more procollagen — not from any 'collagen' ingredient. Topical hydrolyzed collagen is too large to penetrate; it only hydrates the surface.
Topical isoflavones are weak phytoestrogens acting locally; cosmetic use is well-tolerated. Soy allergy and pregnancy are the real caveats, not systemic hormonal effect.

overview: Soy isoflavones firm and even tone by raising procollagen and damping collagen-degrading enzymes, with antioxidant support. Strongest in mature / estrogen-deficient skin; gradual over weeks.

benefits.what_it_means: Helps skin look firmer over weeks. Most evident in mature or post-menopausal skin where natural estrogen support has dropped.
benefits.mechanism: Genistein/daidzein up-regulate type-I procollagen and inhibit MMP-1/MMP-9 (collagen-degrading enzymes) via estrogen-beta signaling.

benefits.what_it_means: Gradually evens tone and brightens; pairs well with niacinamide for the same goal.
benefits.mechanism: Genistein inhibits tyrosinase-driven melanogenesis and scavenges free radicals (antioxidant).

benefits.what_it_means: Supportive, not a retinoid replacement — a gentler antioxidant route for sensitive users.
benefits.mechanism: Reduces UV-induced oxidative stress and MMP induction in dermal fibroblasts.

watchouts.what_to_do: Avoid if allergic to soy; patch test first.
Phytoestrogen — many prefer to avoid as a precaution; defer to a clinician.

consider_separating: high-strength acids (same routine may sting on sensitive skin)
notes: AM use benefits from sunscreen on top (antioxidant supports, does not replace SPF).

evidence.summary: Peer-reviewed mechanism + human/ex-vivo data for isoflavone effects on procollagen, MMPs, and pigmentation. Firming benefit is best-supported in estrogen-deficient skin; cosmetic effect sizes are modest and gradual.
